investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-19T14:50–14:57Z because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. The pod remained Unschedulable for 123–144 seconds until the eval timeout fired, producing zero evidence output and failing every required contract assertion (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState).
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving 0 of 6 nodes available for scheduling. Because the pod never starts, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never completes, no evidence is written, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256) is violated in full. This is an infrastructure capacity or resource-leak condition localized to the remote-agent VM pool, not an eval infrastructure or code defect.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote-agent VMs or peer-pods are consuming all allocatable VM slots, leaving none for new probe pods. Preemption was attempted and found no victims, indicating all current consumers are non-preemptable.
Secondary — resource leak from prior eval runs or user-created remote agents that were not cleaned up, holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots indefinitely and preventing new allocations.

Tertiary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration: the pod's affinity rules restrict scheduling to only 2 nodes (those with kata.peerpods.io/vm), and those 2 nodes are at capacity. If the affinity was recently tightened or nodes were removed from the eligible set, capacity would drop without a change to the VM pool size.
Lower confidence — cluster scale-down or node failure reducing the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes below the level needed to absorb concurrent probe traffic.

If capacity is genuinely exhausted by legitimate workloads, evaluate whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm pool size needs to be increased on the 2 eligible nodes, or whether additional nodes should be added to the eligible set.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl or cluster tooling shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is available and not exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes, the scheduling failure has a different cause (e.g., a quota, admission webhook, or runtime class misconfiguration).

If the pod spec for remote-agent pods does not restrict scheduling to only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes (i.e., the affinity/selector is broader), then the '4 node(s) didn't match' message would indicate a different affinity regression rather than a pure capacity problem.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after freeing no resources succeeds and the pod schedules, the failure was transient (e.g., a brief spike in concurrent VM usage) rather than a sustained exhaustion.

If no existing pods are found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, the resource may be misconfigured or the node plugin may have stopped advertising the resource, which would be a different root cause than exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity across all cluster nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, and fails fast with a capacity-specific message rather than waiting for a pod scheduling timeout.
Add a resource-leak detection eval that periodically inventories all pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and alerts if any have been running longer than the expected maximum remote-agent lifetime.

Add a node-eligibility eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold, catching node pool shrinkage before it causes scheduling failures.

Reduce the remote-agent-create eval's scheduling wait time and surface the Unschedulable reason as structured evidence (e.g., schedulerReason, availableVmSlots) so future failures produce actionable evidence rather than an empty evidence object.

Because the agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the state-polling stage, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was produced and the expected-output contract was fully violated.

The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity/selector constraints. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod request is rejected as Unschedulable before any agent lifecycle work can begin. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval runner or code defect. No evidence of a user-facing incident or real-traffic signal is present in the packet; this is an eval-level failure reflecting the inability to provision a test agent pod.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message reporting that 0 of 6 nodes could schedule the requested pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never completed, no evidence was collected, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. This caused every remote-agent pod creation attempt to remain Unschedulable for the full eval timeout window (123–149 seconds), preventing agent creation, state polling, and runtime chat from executing at all. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity or quota exhaustion event localized to the remote-agent VM node pool, not an application code defect and not a user-traffic incident based on available evidence.

possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: the VM-backed peer-pod resource is a finite, allocatable Kubernetes extended resource. If prior agent pods were not cleaned up, or if concurrent workloads consumed all available VM slots, new pods cannot be scheduled. The scheduler message 'No preemption victims found' confirms no lower-priority pods exist to evict.

[High confidence] Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes in the 6-node cluster satisfy. If those 2 nodes are also resource-exhausted, the effective schedulable pool is zero.

[Medium confidence] Leaked or zombie agent pods from a prior eval run holding kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations: if the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1916) failed to release resources from a previous run, those allocations would persist and reduce available VM capacity.

[Low confidence] Node pool scaling or autoscaler lag: the 2 kata-capable nodes may be undersized for concurrent eval demand, and the cluster autoscaler either is not configured for this node pool or has not yet provisioned additional capacity within the eval timeout window.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-19T14:50–14:57Z because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. The pod remained Unschedulable for 123–144 seconds until the eval timeout fired, producing zero evidence output and failing every required contract assertion (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState).
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving 0 of 6 nodes available for scheduling. Because the pod never starts, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never completes, no evidence is written, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256) is violated in full. This is an infrastructure capacity or resource-leak condition localized to the remote-agent VM pool, not an eval infrastructure or code defect.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote-agent VMs or peer-pods are consuming all allocatable VM slots, leaving none for new probe pods. Preemption was attempted and found no victims, indicating all current consumers are non-preemptable.
Secondary — resource leak from prior eval runs or user-created remote agents that were not cleaned up, holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots indefinitely and preventing new allocations.

Tertiary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration: the pod's affinity rules restrict scheduling to only 2 nodes (those with kata.peerpods.io/vm), and those 2 nodes are at capacity. If the affinity was recently tightened or nodes were removed from the eligible set, capacity would drop without a change to the VM pool size.
Lower confidence — cluster scale-down or node failure reducing the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes below the level needed to absorb concurrent probe traffic.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl or cluster tooling shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is available and not exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes, the scheduling failure has a different cause (e.g., a quota, admission webhook, or runtime class misconfiguration).

If the pod spec for remote-agent pods does not restrict scheduling to only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes (i.e., the affinity/selector is broader), then the '4 node(s) didn't match' message would indicate a different affinity regression rather than a pure capacity problem.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after freeing no resources succeeds and the pod schedules, the failure was transient (e.g., a brief spike in concurrent VM usage) rather than a sustained exhaustion.

If no existing pods are found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, the resource may be misconfigured or the node plugin may have stopped advertising the resource, which would be a different root cause than exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity across all cluster nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, and fails fast with a capacity-specific message rather than waiting for a pod scheduling timeout.
Add a resource-leak detection eval that periodically inventories all pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and alerts if any have been running longer than the expected maximum remote-agent lifetime.

Add a node-eligibility eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold, catching node pool shrinkage before it causes scheduling failures.

Reduce the remote-agent-create eval's scheduling wait time and surface the Unschedulable reason as structured evidence (e.g., schedulerReason, availableVmSlots) so future failures produce actionable evidence rather than an empty evidence object.

possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: the VM-backed peer-pod resource is a finite, allocatable Kubernetes extended resource. If prior agent pods were not cleaned up, or if concurrent workloads consumed all available VM slots, new pods cannot be scheduled. The scheduler message 'No preemption victims found' confirms no lower-priority pods exist to evict.

[High confidence] Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes in the 6-node cluster satisfy. If those 2 nodes are also resource-exhausted, the effective schedulable pool is zero.

[Medium confidence] Leaked or zombie agent pods from a prior eval run holding kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations: if the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1916) failed to release resources from a previous run, those allocations would persist and reduce available VM capacity.

[Low confidence] Node pool scaling or autoscaler lag: the 2 kata-capable nodes may be undersized for concurrent eval demand, and the cluster autoscaler either is not configured for this node pool or has not yet provisioned additional capacity within the eval timeout window.

affectedAreas.reason: Feature registry sets degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2 (lines 187-188). With all 3 checks failing, the feature has crossed both thresholds. remote-agent-runtime is required=false but remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are required=true.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation on the 2 eligible cluster nodes to determine whether capacity is fully consumed and by which pods.
Audit for leaked or zombie remote-agent pods (Pending or Running) that may be holding VM allocations from prior eval runs or user sessions; terminate any that are no longer needed.

If capacity is confirmed exhausted, either increase the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota on existing nodes (if the device plugin supports it) or add additional nodes to the cluster that carry the required node label and kata peer-pod support.

Review the withCleanup wrapper in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs to ensure it reliably releases VM-backed pod resources even on eval timeout or error paths, preventing future resource leaks.

Verify that the node affinity/selector on the remote-agent pod spec is intentional and that the 4 non-matching nodes are correctly excluded; if the affinity is overly restrictive, widening it could increase the schedulable pool.

Monitor the remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state checks (both required=true) as the primary outage signal; the feature has crossed the outageAfterFailures=2 threshold per infra/evals/status/features.json lines 187-188.

Note: this is an eval-layer infrastructure failure. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; do not treat this as a confirmed user-facing outage without additional traffic data.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity available and unallocated on the 2 eligible nodes, the scheduling exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and the cause would shift to a pod spec misconfiguration or API server admission error.

If the remote-agent-runtime eval passed on a re-run immediately after this failure without any infrastructure change, it would suggest a transient scheduling race rather than sustained capacity exhaustion.

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed, the root cause would be localized to the runtime probe's pod spec or resource request rather than a cluster-wide VM capacity problem.
If a different error message (e.g., image pull failure, OOMKilled, API authentication error) appeared on re-run, the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion diagnosis would be incorrect.
If no kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is registered on any node, the failure would indicate a cluster misconfiguration (missing device plugin) rather than capacity exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity across the cluster before attempting remote-agent pod creation, surfacing capacity exhaustion as a distinct 'warn' status rather than a timeout failure.
Add a cluster node-pool health eval that verifies at least N nodes match the remote-agent pod affinity and have non-zero kata.peerpods.io/vm availability, alerting before all capacity is consumed.
Add a leaked-pod detection eval that counts Pending or long-running remote-agent pods and fails if any exceed a configurable age threshold, catching cleanup failures before they exhaust VM quota.
Introduce a separate eval for the kata peer-pod device plugin health (e.g., checking that the DaemonSet is Running on all eligible nodes) to distinguish plugin failures from capacity exhaustion.
Consider adding a historical baseline to the remote-agent-runtime eval run history so that currentlyRegressedFromPass can be computed on future runs, enabling regression detection.
